title: Build a Relevant First Touch
subtitle: Module 5 — Outreach & Engagement

intro.headline: Build a Relevant First Touch
intro.description: A guided mission: decide what earns attention, apply a four-move relevance framework, and build a first touch you can actually use.
bullets: You finish with a saved first-touch draft. Nothing is sent from PartnerOS.

deepDiveTitle: Full Lesson — Build a Relevant First Touch

steps.title: Why should Daniel care?
steps.scenario: Atlas Foods is expanding production. Daniel leads operations. He has probably seen dozens of software messages. What would make this one worth his time?
steps.insight: A first touch earns attention when it makes the next conversation feel relevant before it tries to make the product impressive.

steps.title: Which opening earns the next 20 seconds?

options.label: A
options.text: ManWinWin is a leading CMMS platform with powerful features for maintenance teams.
options.feedback: Credible product information, but it starts with us and asks Daniel to do the relevance work.

options.label: B
options.text: Daniel — expanding production usually puts extra pressure on uptime, planning and spare-parts coordination. Is that one of the operational priorities at Atlas Foods this quarter?
options.feedback: It starts with Daniel's context, connects it to a credible operational issue, and asks a proportionate question. It creates a reason to continue without pretending to know more than the evidence supports.

options.label: C
options.text: I noticed Atlas Foods is growing and thought ManWinWin could be a great fit. Can I show you a demo?
options.feedback: It uses a signal, but jumps from growth to product fit and a demo too quickly.

steps.title: Start with them
steps.body: The buyer should recognize their world before they are asked to understand ours.
bullets: Translate it into a plausible operational implication.
Make the first sentence useful even if they never reply.

items.title: Context
items.question: What verified signal makes this timely?

items.title: Relevance
items.question: What plausible maintenance or operational implication could matter?

items.title: Credibility
items.question: Why is ManWinWin or the partner relevant to this conversation?

items.title: Next Step
items.question: What small, useful action is proportionate now?

steps.title: Evidence before assumption
steps.prompt: Atlas Foods has announced a new production line. Which sentence goes beyond the evidence?

options.label: A
options.text: A new line may increase coordination demands across maintenance and operations.

options.label: B
options.text: The expansion could make planning, asset data and spare-parts visibility more important.

options.label: C
options.text: Atlas Foods is currently losing 14 hours of production every month because its CMMS is outdated.

options.label: D
options.text: It may be useful to understand how the maintenance team is preparing for the additional asset load.

steps.correctFeedback: Correct. The 14-hour loss and outdated-CMMS claim are unsupported. Relevant outreach can interpret a verified signal, but it cannot invent operational facts.
steps.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. Look for the sentence that turns a plausible implication into a specific, unverified fact.

steps.title: Turn context into business relevance
steps.prompt: Choose the best first-touch sentence for Daniel.

options.label: Brochure
options.text: ManWinWin includes preventive maintenance, inventory, work orders and reporting.
options.feedback: This is a brochure. It is accurate, but it starts with the product instead of Daniel's situation.

options.label: Mind Reader
options.text: Your maintenance team is struggling to control downtime during the expansion.
options.feedback: This assumes a problem the evidence does not support. Assumption presented as fact damages credibility.

options.label: Creepy
options.text: I saw your LinkedIn post at 08:42 and noticed three Atlas Foods employees viewed our page.
options.feedback: Surveillance detail feels invasive. Relevance is about their business context, not their digital footprint.

options.label: Relevant
options.text: Daniel — with Atlas Foods adding a new production line, maintenance planning and asset readiness may become more important. How are you preparing for that operationally?
options.feedback: This is relevant, not invasive or assumptive. It uses a verified public signal, offers a plausible implication rather than an invented fact, and asks a proportionate question Daniel can easily answer.

steps.reasoningPrompt: Why does this option work? Select every reason that applies.

reasoningOptions.text: It starts with a verified business signal.
It connects the signal to a plausible operational implication.
It proves ManWinWin is the best CMMS.
It asks for a small, relevant next step.
It creates urgency by assuming a problem.

steps.reasoningFeedback: Option D works because it is relevant — grounded in a verified signal, plausible rather than assumptive, and proportionate in what it asks. It never claims to know Daniel's problems and never relies on invasive detail.

steps.title: Ask for the smallest useful next step
steps.prompt: Which next step creates the least friction while still moving the conversation forward?

options.label: A
options.text: Can you send your full asset register so I can prepare a proposal?

options.label: B
options.text: Can we book a 60-minute demo with operations, maintenance and IT?

options.label: C
options.text: Would a 15-minute exchange on how you are preparing maintenance for the new line be useful?

steps.correctFeedback: Exactly. It is specific, relevant and easy to accept or decline.
steps.incorrectFeedback: The best first step should reduce commitment, not accelerate the buying process before relevance is established.

steps.title: Use AI without outsourcing judgement
steps.prompt: Draft a concise first-touch message for Daniel at Atlas Foods using only the verified expansion signal and the four-move framework. Clearly label any assumption.
steps.rule: AI drafts. Evidence anchors. Human approves.

steps.title: Mission Takeaway
steps.quote: The first touch sells the conversation. Not the product.
bullets: Relevance starts with the buyer's context.
Business value should be plausible, not invented.
The next step should be proportionate.
